notes:
I couldn't do any research on Psalm 143, so I have no notes for you yet. My first attempt to open the source pages failed with a message saying I had no code-execution calls left for this turn, and a second, smaller attempt got the same error. Search and page-reading only work through that tool, and the other tool I have can't reach the internet.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. So I haven't written any notes from memory, not even for the parts I know well.

**What I'll do when you ask again (in a new message, so the tool limit resets):**
- **Verse by verse:** enduringword.com (Guzik), biblehub.com (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary) and preceptaustin.org.
- **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, and Lutheran and Reformed teachers. The main focus would be v. 2 ("no one alive is righteous before You") and what each tradition says it means for how God declares people righteous. I'll only report differences the sources actually state.
- **Other views:**
  - **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org translation notes.
  - **Catholic:** Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org, where this psalm is numbered 142.
  - **Orthodox:** oca.org, where this psalm is read at the start of Matins.
  - **Popular modern teaching:** any material on these sites, if it exists.
